Subject: Re: Unexpected throughput drop / 503s this morning

Hi Vanessa,

We started seeing a sharp drop in throughput and a series of 503s hitting our production traffic starting ~08:45 PST. Our ops dashboard shows p95 jumping from ~160ms to ~1.4s and p99 up around 4.1–4.6s for the last 30 minutes. Affected endpoints are the hosted text-generation route we call (model: rdx-large-v1).

I attached a small sample of request IDs and traces (novaresco_sample_requests.json). We’re seeing repeated token stalls — some requests emit a few tokens then hang and finally time out with 503. This is causing downstream retries that amplify the load. Can you escalate to engineering? We need an ETA and whether we should failover to the dedicated pool (we don’t have an automated policy for that).

This is impacting a production flow (billing-related) and we may need exec engagement if this is going to be prolonged.

Thanks,
Elaine

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.ai>

Subject: Re: Unexpected throughput drop / 503s this morning — initial findings

Vanessa / team — quick update from infra/runtime: we’ve been seeing a correlated pattern across several serving nodes hosting rdx-large-v1 where memory allocator fragmentation grows after long-running sessions. Symptoms: transient allocation failures, internal runtime retries, and on a subset of hosts a kernel-level OOM that restarts the inference worker causing in-flight requests to return 503.

Evidence:
- Attach: runtime-dump-20261130.tar.gz (heap snapshots and allocator logs)
- Host metrics show repeated small spikes in GPU memory usage followed by drops consistent with worker restarts (host-metrics-aggregated.csv).

Root-cause hypothesis: fragmentation in our custom allocator + insufficient compaction frequency under token-streaming workloads (many long-lived sessions + KV cache growth). The allocator fails to coalesce free blocks which eventually yields transient OOMs for larger attention windows.

Immediate mitigations (30–60m):
1) Drain and restart the 6 most affected hosts (non-disruptive to region if we shift traffic) — rolling drain in 10m waves.
2) Temporarily lower the per-request max-batch size and disable long-lived batching on NovaResco routes to avoid large contiguous allocations.
3) Enable aggressive KV cache eviction (reduce warm threshold) for their tenant to cap memory growth.

Short-term deploy (1–3h):
- Push a small runtime patch that forces periodic compaction and fixes one allocator path; staged rollout to 10% hosts then 100% if metrics look good.

I’ll start drains now and apply the route overrides. Will report p95/p99 after the first wave.

—Rishi
Senior Engineering Manager, Inference Runtime

Status update — final: we completed the rolling drain and restarted the most affected hosts at ~11:05 PST, applied the temporary routing overrides, and saw p99 drop from ~4.4s to ~220ms within the first 35m. After staging the runtime compaction patch on 10% of hosts and observing no regressions, we rolled to 100% by 15:50 PST. Post-deploy metrics: p95 ~170ms, p99 ~360ms (within expected variance). Error rate (503) is back to baseline.

Next steps:
- Post-mortem will include allocator root-cause analysis, a longer-term fix for the allocator path, and improved host-level OOM detection and automated failover rules.
- We will share a detailed incident report and remediation timeline by EOD tomorrow and propose a customer credit per Marissa's recommendation.

Attachments: runtime-dump-20261130.tar.gz, host-metrics-aggregated.csv (already shared).

Thanks for patience, Elaine — we’ll follow up with the post-mortem.
